insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution; this protocol settles verified purchase events at ~$0.10 each — a 50–200x cost gap that isn't a feature comparison, it's a structural replacement of the attribution problem itself.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the industry has no cross-ecosystem, identity-free signal that confirms a purchase actually occurred — verified receipts fill exactly that void.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other — and neither can sell you a cross-ecosystem view without identity liability; a protocol producing aggregate verified signals without PII is the only architecture that solves this.

Receipts classified as 'Unknown' represent 10% of 14-day volume but 34.7% of 14-day GMV ($269 average ticket vs. $46–$55 for grocery, restaurant, and retail), suggesting high-value purchase categories — likely electronics, luxury, or specialty — are flowing through the protocol untagged and underexploited for targeting.

Adoption is expanding via social graph propagation, not paid acquisition — simultaneous activation in non-contiguous non-metro markets (Hawaii, rural CA, AR, MI, MA in the same cycle) means the verified signal base is reaching demographics and geographies that traditional digital targeting consistently underindexes.

7-day GMV has oscillated in a $29–$34K band rather than compounding, and velocity has repeatedly approached but not sustained a break above 0.8x — cumulative growth is real, but marketers evaluating scale should treat weekly throughput as range-bound until a multi-cycle hold above that threshold is confirmed.
